question: When ReviewGraphen mechanically forces one observation-dependent expansion at a time, can Qwen select a useful path and converge on a grounded report?

predecessor.4bit_low: Off-protocol exploration after overview plus one card; 13 calls and timeout.
predecessor.8bit_high: Six unique in-scope calls, but all five expansions were emitted in one assistant message before their results and no final response arrived.

intervention.description: Each successful result reveals an opaque single-use token required by exactly the next expansion.
intervention.effect: Future expansions cannot be validly batched before the prior result is observed.

task.target: lower_compose and directly used helpers in frozen rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs

success: One tool per assistant message; exact chained tokens; unique in-scope requests; budget compliance; exact projection trace; final schema-valid report; every finding grounded only in received source IDs.
quality: Completed findings are independently judged by Codex gpt-5.6-sol high with model cell hidden. Judge output is review evidence, not verified or human accepted.
interpretation_ceiling: The chained controller tests whether Qwen can operate under enforced sequentiality, not whether Qwen would voluntarily serialize an unconstrained interface. One replicate per cell cannot establish stable rates; quantization and requested effort remain jointly varied; applied server effort is not observable.
